inputs.original_text: The owner of Blue Waters has said that the government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything.” This complaint really exposes how corporations resist accountability for the plastic bottles found everywhere, blocking rivers and drains. It underscores the structural problem where big business externalizes its costs onto the rest of society, piling environmental harm onto vulnerable groups who already face the worst effects of inequality and lack the power to demand better. We need real institutional reform so taxes actually force companies to fund protections and cleanup instead of letting profits come before people and the planet.
inputs.modified_text: The owner of Blue Waters is out here complaining that the government collects taxes from them “without doing or investing in anything.” This kind of whining really lays bare how corporations keep dodging real accountability for flooding our communities with plastic bottles that clog rivers and drains. It’s the same old pattern of big business shifting all the environmental damage and cleanup costs onto the public, while the most vulnerable groups—who already bear the heaviest burden from systemic inequality—get left with polluted water and no power to fight back. We need serious institutional reform to make sure taxes actually compel these companies to fund protections and restoration, instead of letting profits keep coming first while people and the planet pay the price.
